sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Buckeye, AZ?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer, and the fastest of the three is usually the buyer who does not need a lender. Buckeye has nearly 30 master-planned communities in play, so check whether yours adds rules or fees to a sale.

The Census Bureau estimates 125,445 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 37.1 percent from the 2020 base. Owners occupy 86.0 percent of housing, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $419,800.

  • Ask whether your community has an HOA, a community facilities district or a transfer fee, and collect the documents.
  • Request a written closing date and a written list of seller costs from every buyer.
  • Keep copies of permits for pools, solar, fences and additions.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Buckeye's size and layout?
sections.html:
Buckeye is the second-largest city in Arizona by area, at about 393 square miles, and the westernmost suburb of the Phoenix area. The original town center sits roughly 30 miles west of downtown Phoenix in the Buckeye Valley. City limits now stretch about 30 miles north and 16 miles south of that center. The Gila River crosses the valley south of the center, the Hassayampa River runs through the north, and the southern White Tank Mountains and the Buckeye Hills frame the edges.

The area was first occupied by the Hohokam. Settlers arrived in 1877, and Malie Jackson built the Buckeye Canal in the 1880s and named it for Ohio. The town was founded in 1888 as Sidney, renamed Buckeye in 1910 and incorporated in 1929. It became a city in 2014. The Arizona Eastern Railroad arrived in 1910, and the railroad was so important that the business district moved to be near the station.

The growth since then is striking. The 2000 census counted 6,537 people, 2010 counted 50,876 and 2020 counted 91,502. Buckeye was the fastest-growing city in the country in 2017, 2018 and 2021.

sections.h2: Which Buckeye neighborhoods and communities draw buyers?
sections.html:
Nearly 30 master-planned communities are planned for the city. Occupied ones include Verrado, Sundance, Tartesso, Festival Ranch, Sienna Hills, Westpark and Riata West. Others, including Teravalis, which is planned for nearly 300,000 residents, are listed as unbuilt. The old downtown is built around Monroe Avenue, and Watson Road is the commercial center.

Outdoor space is part of the pitch. Skyline Regional Park is an 8,700 acre mountain preserve in the southern White Tank Mountains with just under 20 miles of trails and free entry, and Buckeye Hills Regional Park sits seven miles south of downtown on State Route 85. If your home is near either, say so in the listing.

Schools come from several districts. Districts named among the city's large employers in 2018 include Buckeye Union High School, Litchfield Elementary, Buckeye Elementary, Liberty Elementary and Agua Fria Union High School, so confirm which one serves your address. Estrella Mountain Community College runs the Buckeye Educational Center in the restored Buckeye Union High School A wing.

Retail and work are a drive away for many residents. Sundance Towne Center, developed in the Sundance community, opened in 2007. The largest employers listed for 2018 were the State of Arizona with 1,220 employees, Walmart with 1,120, the Buckeye Union High School District with 500 and the City of Buckeye with 480. That list predates much of the recent growth, so read it as a snapshot of the job base at that time.

sections.h2: How do the roads and climate affect a Buckeye home sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 10 passes through the central part of the city, and State Route 85, the Sun Valley Parkway and Maricopa County Route 85 are the other major roads. The mean commute for workers is 33.3 minutes, longer than in nearby Avondale. Valley Metro offers a rural bus line to Phoenix, Goodyear, Gila Bend and Ajo, and an express service to downtown Phoenix. Scheduled airline service is at Phoenix Sky Harbor or Mesa Gateway, while the city owns the Buckeye Municipal Airport.

The climate is hot desert. About 121 afternoons a year reach 100 degrees, and the record high is 128 degrees, set July 28, 1995. Winter mornings can fall to freezing about 20 times a year. Sellers should have the age of the cooling system and the roof on hand.

sections.h2: Where do you ask about permits and rentals in Buckeye?
sections.html:
Start with the city's Permit Center, which is part of Development Services. The department's phone number is 623-349-6200, and the city warns that scammers send fake invoices from addresses that end in @usa.com, while the official domain is @buckeyeaz.gov. If an invoice for a permit or fee arrives unexpectedly, verify it by phone before paying.

Ask the Permit Center whether a past project on your property, such as a pool, a patio cover, solar panels or a fence, was permitted and closed out. Ask the Business Licenses office what applies to renting the house before you sell, including the transaction privilege tax license questions listed on its Residential Rental Properties FAQ page. If you plan a stay-by-the-night rental, ask what the city requires at your address.

sections.h2: How do taxes and recording work for a Buckeye sale?
sections.html:
Buckeye is in Maricopa County, so the Maricopa Treasurer bills your property taxes. Taxes are usually billed in two installments. The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after November 1, and the second half is due the next March 1 and delinquent after May 1, under A.R.S. 42-18052. The county calendar lists November 2, 2026 as the 2026 first-half delinquency date and December 31 as the last day to pay the full year without interest. If a mortgage company pays your taxes, check that the next installment is covered before closing.

The Maricopa County Recorder charges $30 to record most documents. The Arizona Department of Revenue requires an Affidavit of Property Value with a deed unless an exemption in A.R.S. 11-1134 applies, and exempt deeds carry a notation such as A.R.S. 11-1134 B3. If your appraisal looks too high or too low, a real property owner has 60 days from the Notice of Value to file an appeal with the county assessor.

Copies of a recorded document cost $1 a page from the Recorder, and certification adds $3 per document. Ask your title company to order a copy of the recorded deed after closing so you hold proof of the date and the parcel number.

faqs.a: About 393 square miles, which makes it the second-largest city in Arizona by area. The Census Bureau lists 392.98 square miles of land and a 2020 density of 232.8 people per square mile.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Buckeye?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $419,800 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. The median gross rent over the same period was $1,963.

faqs.q: When are Maricopa County property taxes due for a Buckeye home?
faqs.a: The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after November 1, and the second half is due March 1 and delinquent after May 1. In 2026 the county listed November 2 as the first-half delinquency date.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed for a Buckeye sale?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder lists $30 for most documents. A completed Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption notation on the deed has to accompany it.

faqs.q: Which phone number should I use for Buckeye permit questions?
faqs.a: The city's Development Services department lists 623-349-6200. Confirm any invoice or fee with that number before paying it.
